hypothesis: Remove the premature finite-budget state-space cutoff by raising only the fixed molecular heavy-atom safety ceiling, allowing the same persistent chain to continue drawing fresh single-fragment reversible edits instead of aborting when its 80-heavy-atom deletion neighborhood has been consumed.
method_thesis: Extract a vocabulary of single-attachment fragments from the allowed unlabeled corpus without scoring or retrieving any whole corpus molecule, and start one persistent molecular-graph Markov chain from each of the ten fixed evaluated molecules. In every feedback round, generate one fresh candidate per chain through a locally sanitized, reversible fragment-add or fragment-delete transition, retrying locally until the batch contains ten novel canonical molecules. After the oracle returns, accept each proposed state with a Metropolis-Hastings probability for an annealed score density, including its forward/reverse proposal ratio; rejected proposals leave their chains at the previous states. Low inverse temperature initially permits controlled downhill moves that can cross structural valleys, while increasing concentration later favors high-score states. Thus all oracle calls evaluate de novo molecular constructions, and feedback directly steers persistent search paths toward a stronger final Top-1 without a surrogate, a learned generator, or finite-library screening.

method_tags.acquisition_mechanism: annealed score-density ratio with forward/reverse proposal correction
method_tags.learning_mechanism: training-free root in which oracle feedback updates chain states and annealed target concentration rather than model parameters
method_tags.proposal_mechanism: reversible fragment-add/delete transitions from persistent chains followed by per-chain Metropolis-Hastings accept/reject
method_tags.representation: explicit RDKit molecular graphs with corpus-derived single-attachment fragments

applicability_conditions: The repair applies to the recorded failure in which repeated accepted fragment additions drive chains to the implementation-only 80-heavy-atom ceiling, after which novelty filtering can exhaust the remaining deletion endpoints before the fixed 300-call budget is complete.

The fixed initial panel, ten-chain batch assignment, at most 29 adaptive transitions per chain, and at most 12 heavy atoms per attached vocabulary fragment bound every reachable chain below the repaired 400-heavy-atom ceiling during this evaluation profile.

The repair does not claim to recover exhaustion caused by an empty fragment vocabulary, invalid initial molecules, or absence of any structurally reversible add/delete endpoint independent of the former size ceiling.
research_intent.falsifier: The repair is falsified if any seed-0 objective again raises the recorded per-chain novel-reversible-edit RuntimeError before 300 oracle calls, emits a batch other than the announced size 10, or produces a candidate outside the unchanged single-fragment add/delete construction path.
research_intent.implementation_change: Change only MAX_MOLECULE_HEAVY_ATOMS from 80 to 400. Leave fragment extraction, uniform raw add/delete sampling, forward and reverse probability calculations, global and within-batch novelty filtering, persistent chain assignment, annealing, Metropolis-Hastings decisions, telemetry, and protocol handling unchanged.
research_intent.mechanism: Remove the premature finite-budget state-space cutoff by raising only the fixed molecular heavy-atom safety ceiling, allowing the same persistent chain to continue drawing fresh single-fragment reversible edits instead of aborting when its 80-heavy-atom deletion neighborhood has been consumed.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: Algorithm Node n-718111259202 completed 19 ten-molecule adaptive batches on every seed-0 objective, then every task exited at 200 oracle calls when chain 6 could not produce another novel reversible edit under the 80-heavy-atom ceiling and permanent novelty filter.

applicability_conditions: The evidence directly supports the recorded ceiling-driven failure mode. Under the Parent's 80-heavy-atom guard, all ten chain states on every objective ended generation 18 at exactly 80 heavy atoms and the next batch exhausted chain 6; under the isolated 400-heavy-atom guard, each objective emitted 191 candidates above 80 heavy atoms and completed all 29 batches.

Causal isolation is strong for this recovery: the formal Candidate differs from the Parent only in MAX_MOLECULE_HEAVY_ATOMS changing from 80 to 400. Fragment preparation, seeded random draws, raw add/delete construction, proposal arithmetic, novelty filtering, retry guard, persistent state updates, annealing, diagnostics, and evaluator protocol are source-identical.

The repaired ceiling was ample for this evaluation profile. Across all five completed task sessions the largest logged canonical Candidate had 168 heavy atoms, and even the last generation's resulting chain states ranged only from 130 to 168 heavy atoms, leaving substantial room below 400.

Operational support is for the observed nonempty 64-fragment vocabulary, ten sanitizable initial chains, batch size 10, and at most 29 adaptive transitions per chain. Within that setting every Candidate batch required only 11 to 29 raw edit draws in total for its ten emissions, and no chain approached the inherited 2,500-local-attempt guard.

The recovery does not establish a remedy for an empty or chemically unusable fragment vocabulary, invalid initial molecules, or a chain with no structurally reversible add/delete endpoint independent of molecular size; none of those excluded conditions occurred in this replica.

This node confirms removal of the premature 80-heavy-atom state-space cutoff and full-budget execution only. It does not overturn the Parent analysis that permanent novelty filtering removes evaluated parents from the emitted reverse support and that the logged raw proposal probabilities omit retry-until-survivor conditioning; those inherited methodological limitations remain outside this bounded repair.
Evidence is limited to screening seed 0 on the five frozen objectives. It establishes activation and completion for this replica, not independent-seed reliability or competitive score quality.

observable_measurements.value: Seed 0 completed the full registered workload on all five objectives (zaleplon_mpo, deco_hop, drd2_docking, median_2, and sitagliptin_mpo). Each Candidate task log contains generations 0 through 28: 29/29 complete adaptive generation records, every record has emitted = announced_batch_size = 10, and every generation has ten matching offspring and ten scored-transition records. Thus each task emitted 290 adaptive candidates and reached 300 total oracle calls; across the replica this is 145 complete batches, 1,450 adaptive candidates, and 1,500 calls. Every task summary reports status ok, proposal_attempts = accepted_attempts = 290, valid_rate = 1.0, and duplicate_attempts = 0. No Candidate task log contains a Traceback, RuntimeError, or novelty-exhaustion exception. At the exact former failure point, line 421 of every Candidate task log records generation 19 successfully emitting 10/10 molecules from 21 raw edit draws; the sessions then complete through generation 28 and cleanly shut down at line 641 with generations = 29. All 1,450 offspring records remain on the unchanged single-fragment path: each names one add-or-delete operation, one vocabulary fragment, its chain and evaluated parent, an attachment record, and the reconstructed opposite operation; the records comprise 1,200 additions and 250 deletions.
